# Demox
> Demox is a static website deployment platform for frontend builds, AI-generated pages, and documents. It provides public links through web, CLI, MCP, and API workflows without requiring users to configure servers, CDN, HTTPS, or cache policies.

## Primary pages
- [Demox homepage](https://www.demox.site/): Product overview and web deployment entry point.
- [CLI and MCP documentation](https://www.demox.site/doc): Installation, authentication, deployment commands, supported inputs, and FAQ.
- [Pricing](https://www.demox.site/pricing): Current Demox plans.
- [Changelog](https://www.demox.site/log): Product and infrastructure updates.

## Developer resources
- [Demox repository](https://github.com/demox-site/demox): Main web application and platform source.
- [Demox agent skill](https://github.com/demox-site/skill): Instructions for deploying with an AI coding agent.
- CLI package: `@demox-site/cli`
- MCP package: `@demox-site/mcp-server`

## Supported deployment inputs
- Static build directories and ZIP archives with `index.html` at the root
- Standalone HTML pages
- PDF, Markdown, TXT, and DOCX documents
- Spreadsheet files supported by the web upload workflow

## Key distinction
Demox is for fast static delivery when someone needs a link they can open. It does not claim to replace a full CI/CD platform such as Vercel or Netlify.

This optional file helps documentation-oriented AI tools navigate Demox resources. Google Search states that `llms.txt` does not affect Google Search or its generative AI features.
